linkedin.title: The biggest problem with the news today is not that we have too little of it.
linkedin.body:
It is that we have too much. Most of us are drowning in a constant stream of headlines that do not actually matter to our daily lives or our specific interests. We end up skimming everything and retaining almost nothing.

True information intake should not feel like a chore. It should be about finding the signal in the noise. When you filter out the irrelevant clutter, you stop just consuming content and start actually learning.

Personalisation is not about creating an echo chamber where you only hear what you already agree with. It is about efficiency. It is about having a tool that understands what topics you care about deeply and delivering the most important updates on those subjects, without the filler.

When we curate our own inputs, we become better informed citizens. We spend less time scrolling aimlessly and more time understanding the stories that shape our world.

story_card.headline: Neptune’s strange moon setup explained
story_card.standfirst: Scientists are solving the mystery of why Neptune has one massive moon and many tiny ones.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Neptune has a weird imbalance. Its largest moon, Triton, holds 99% of the planet's satellite mass.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Triton orbits backward compared to Neptune's rotation. This suggests it was captured by the planet.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This capture likely caused chaos, destroying other moons and shaping the current ring system.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Researchers are using this data to map out how Neptune's moon system evolved over time.

story_card.caption:
Scientists are studying how Neptune captured its massive moon Triton and destroyed its original moon system.

Triton is a total outlier in the solar system. Its backward orbit and massive size compared to the tiny moons around it hint at a violent history where Neptune snagged it from space. This capture likely wiped out previous satellites.

Do you think there are other captured moons out there waiting to be discovered?
